facts.statement: The genus Nankangia was first described by Lü et al. in 2013.
Fossils of Nankangia are found in the Upper Cretaceous Nanxiong Formation in southeastern China.
facts.quote: known from the Upper Cretaceous Nanxiong Formation of Nankang County, Ganzhou City of Jiangxi Province, southeastern China

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was discovered in 2010 by a local farmer in Longling town and donated to the Ganzhou Museum of Natural History.
facts.quote: The holotype was found in 2010 at the town of Longling of Nankang, Ganzhou City, by a local farmer who donated it to the Ganzhou Museum of Natural History

facts.statement: The fossils date to the Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: It was collected from the Nanxiong Formation, dating probably to the Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous
Its diet consisted of leaves and seeds

facts.statement: Its short lower jaw and non-downturned jaw joint suggest it was likely more herbivorous than carnivorous.
facts.quote: The relatively short dentary and non-downturned mandibular symphysis of Nankangia suggest that it may have been more herbivorous than carnivorous

facts.statement: The femoral neck extends dorsomedially at about 90 degrees to the shaft.
facts.quote: Its femoral neck extends dorsomedially at about 90° to the shaft

facts.statement: The ilium of Nankangia is uniquely shaped and resembles the ilia of Chirostenotes, Rinchenia, Heyuannia, and Shixinggia.
facts.quote: The ilium of Nankangia is uniquely shaped, and among oviraptorosaurians, resembles the ilia of Chirostenotes, Rinchenia, Heyuannia and Shixinggia

facts.statement: Nankangia has a U-shaped mandibular symphysis, unlike the V-shaped one found in Luoyanggia.
facts.quote: Unlike the V-shaped mandibular symphysis of Luoyanggia, Nankangia and other oviraptorosaurs have a U-shaped mandibular symphysis

facts.statement: A 2017 analysis recovered Nankangia as an oviraptorid closely related to Yulong and Nomingia.
facts.quote: The phylogenetic analysis of Lü et al. (2017) recovered it as an oviraptorid closely related to Yulong and Nomingia

facts.statement: A 2022 analysis found Nankangia to be the most basal oviraptorid.
facts.quote: the phylogenetic analysis of Wei et al. (2022) found it to be the most basal oviraptorid

facts.statement: Nankangia lived between 72.2 and 66 million years ago during the Maastrichtian.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Nankangia is an extinct genus of caenagnathoid oviraptorosaurian dinosaur.
